relevance_note: Case report of one patient with a diagnosis of fish-eye disease, a partial LCAT deficiency: 'the patient was diagnosed with FED'; no LCAT variant is reported.
method_note: Hand extraction of a short case report. The proband ('patient', rule 5) was diagnosed with FED on biochemical grounds (HDL, LDL, free/esterified cholesterol ratio, LCAT activity); the paper reports no genetic testing and prints no LCAT variant, so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported (defined as patients with a LCAT variant) is null. Her maternal great-grandfather is included as an affected relative (bilateral corneal opacifications); no diagnosis is stated for him. 'No relevant history in her paternal family' describes no individual, so no rows. Two previously published FED patients described individually in the Discussion are included: the French patient of Koster et al. (ref 7; 'cornea appeared thick') and the Japanese patient of Tateno et al. (ref 5; central corneal thicknesses 507 and 510 um); labels use the reference number as printed (superscript ^7, ^5). Barchiesi, Viestenz and Palmiero (Table 1, refs 2, 8, 9) are described only as 'patients with LCAT deficiency' at group level, so no rows. The Discussion's general statements that FED patients lack anemia and renal disease are not used for any person. 'No other abnormal findings in the anterior or posterior segment' is a whole-examination normal statement and excludes nothing specific; not recorded. Free cholesterol 74.0 mg/dl is given only as part of a 'high free cholesterol to esterified cholesterol ratio'; recorded as reduced cholesteryl ester fraction (observed) but 'elevated unesterified (free) cholesterol' left not reported because the absolute level is not called elevated. Chronic kidney disease or renal failure marked excluded from 'renal function was preserved (no proteinuria)'. Age at diagnosis not stated explicitly (36 years is the age at referral) and left not reported. No contradictions found.
